 Advertisement New Hampshire Food Bank says need for food high as holidays approach
 Advertisement Updated: 7:45 PM EST Nov 18, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Maria Wilson Reporter New Hampshire Food Bank says need for food high as holidays approach
 Updated: 7:45 PM EST Nov 18, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Maria Wilson Reporter MANCHESTER, N.H. — The New Hampshire Food Bank is expecting that more people will need its help putting food on the table this holiday season.
 Officials at the food bank said food insecurity affects roughly 11% of Granite Staters, and with food costing more these days, it can be an added stress to the holiday season. 
 Advertisement Food bank officials said one out of every six children in New Hampshire is facing food insecurity. It's a struggle all year long and especially during the holiday season.
 "Food pantries used to be the secondary source, the supplemental source for families and individuals facing food insecurity in New Hampshire," said executive director Elsy Cipriani. "We are seeing more and more food pantries are becoming the primary source of food for families and individuals to survive on a weekly basis because of the high cost of living."
 Cipriani said the food bank is working extra hard this season due to increased need compared to previous years. 
 "Many of our partner agencies keep sharing with us that they are serving two times, three times the number of people that they were serving last year," she said. "That is a challenge for them, because most of us are working with the same resources, trying to do more with less."
 The food bank works with more than 400 partners across the state to families can enjoy a hot meal on the table in time for Thanksgiving.
